headline: ScientistTwo reports an end-to-end automated research workflow, with quality claims resting on AI review
summary: Nam et al. describe ScientistTwo, a multi-agent workflow that takes research questions and accepted-paper baselines through idea generation, experiments, ablations and manuscript drafting. On 107 benchmark specifications derived from accepted ICLR 2026, NeurIPS 2025 and ICML 2026 papers, the authors report 86 successful executions (80.4%). They report that generated manuscripts scored above accepted-paper averages on ScholarPeer and Stanford Agentic Reviewer for ICLR 2026 and NeurIPS 2025. These ratings come from two automated reviewers, not an independent human expert panel; they do not establish novelty, expert-level discovery or real conference acceptance. The paper also states that its AutoSOTA comparison is not head-to-head because hardware and metrics differ.
